VI.description: This example demonstrates how to continuously generate an analog output waveform by providing new data to the output buffer as the task is running.\0A\0AThis example is useful if you want to generate a non-repeating waveform\2C make updates on-the-fly\2C or generate a frequency that is not an even divide-down of your sample clock. In this example\2C the default frequency value is 17 to demonstrate that non-regenerative output can be used to create a signal with a frequency that is not an even divide-down of your sample clock.

Indicator.description: Actual Sample Rate returns the coerced value of the sample clock.\0A\0AIf using OnboardClock as your Sample Clock Source\2C your hardware will attempt to derive the sample clock from one of its internal timebases. If it is unable to derive the exact frequency you require\2C the rate will be coerced.

Control.description: Physical Channel(s) specifies the names of the physical channels to use to create virtual channels. The DAQmx physical channel constant lists all physical channels on devices and modules installed in the system.\0A\0ATo specify a range of physical channels\2C use a colon between two channel numbers or two physical channel names\3A\0A Dev1/ao0\3A3\0A Dev1/ao0\3ADev1/ao3\0A\0AYou can specify channel ranges in reverse order\3A\0A Dev1/ao4\3A0\0A\0AUse commas to separate physical channel names and ranges in a list as follows\3A\0A Dev1/ao0\2C Dev1/ao2\3A3

Min Voltage specifies the minimum value you will generate.\0A\0AThis value is used to help determine the range of the DAC. The actual range will be coerced to one that your hardware supports. Refer to your device documentation for a list of available ranges.

Max Voltage specifies the maximum value you expect to generate.\0A\0AThis value is used to help determine the range of the DAC. The actual range will be coerced to one that your hardware supports. Refer to your device documentation for a list of available ranges.
Sample Clock Source specifies the source terminal of the Sample Clock.\0A\0ARefer to the Device Routes table in Measurement and Automation Explorer to determine eligible sample clock sources.
Sample Rate specifies the sampling rate in samples per channel per second. If you use an external source for the Sample Clock\2C set this input to the maximum expected rate of that clock.

Control.description: Edge specifies on which edge of the digital signal to start acquiring or generating samples.

Digital Trigger Source specifies the name of a terminal where there is a digital signal to use as the source of the trigger.\0A\0ARefer to the Device Routes table in Measurement and Automation Explorer to determine eligible trigger sources.
Slope specifies on which slope of the signal to start acquiring or generating samples when the signal crosses the desired level.

Hysteresis adds a window above or below the trigger level and often is used to reduce false triggering due to noise or jitter in the signal. \0A\0AWhen using hysteresis with a rising slope\2C the trigger asserts when the signal starts below the trigger level minus hysteresis and then crosses above level. The trigger deasserts when the signal crosses below level minus hysteresis.

Level specifies at what threshold to start acquiring or generating samples. Specify this value in the units of the measurement or generation. Use slope to specify on which slope to trigger at this threshold.

Analog Trigger Source is the name of a virtual channel or terminal where there is an analog signal to use as the source of the trigger.\0A\0AIf you specify a virtual channel\2C all values will be in the engineering units (EU) of this virtual channel. If you specify a terminal\2C all values will be in volts (V). \0A\0ANot all hardware supports analog triggering. Refer to your device documentation for information on valid trigger sources. \0A\0ASome examples include\3A\0A APFI0\0A Dev1/ai0

Pause When specifies the state of the digital line that pauses the acquisition.

FreeLabel.comment: Why is there a Wait (ms)?\0A\0ABecause the cDAQ-918x chassis communicates over Ethernet\2C the host can write data faster than the device can generate it. This causes the Ethernet buffer to fill ahead of the actual output\2C leading to a delay when the user changes parameters such as amplitude or frequency. Adding a Wait(ms) equal to (Number of Samples / Sample Rate) x 1000 slows the write loop so the buffer does not get too far ahead. This improves update responsiveness\2C but Ethernet latency spikes may still cause issues. The more robust method is to limit DAQmx Write to only two buffer lengths ahead of the actual generation\2C as described in knowledge base \3A\0A\0A 1. Ethernet cDAQ Not Sending On-the-Fly Updates for Analog Output \0A 2. How to Decrease the Update Delay with Analog Output in a cDAQ 9188
Not all hardware supports all trigger types.\0ARefer to your device documentation for more information.
